items.abstract: <jats:p>Contemporary agentic AI systems face critical challenges in tool orchestration, dynamic coordination, and framework interoperability. I present FATA (Framework Agnostic and Task Agnostic Agentic AI), a novel control plane design pattern that enables scalable, distributed multi-agent orchestration through serverless architecture. FATA introduces a unified tool management layer that dynamically routes, validates, and governs tool interactions while maintaining framework independence. My approach distinguishes between specialized AI agents for targeted automation and collaborative agentic ecosystems with emergent collective intelligence. Through systematic evaluation across cybersecurity, compliance, and document processing domains, FATA demonstrates the capability to reduce developer complexity, enable runtime adaptability, and provide robust governance mechanisms for enterprise-scale agentic deployments.</jats:p>
title: FATA: A Framework-Agnostic, Task-Agnostic Agentic AI Platform for Serverless Multi-Agent Orchestration

items.abstract: <jats:p>The term "agentic AI" has become the most overused phrase in enterprise software marketing. Every vendor now claims autonomous agents, yet most offerings amount to linear prompt chains wrapped in a loop. This paper separates the engineering reality from the vendor hype, presenting an architectural framework for deploying multi-agent systems across private equity deal workflows-from sourcing through investment committee preparation-with the verification patterns, failure modes, and human escalation protocols that production deployment actually requires. Drawing on Anthropic's published research demonstrating 90.2% outperformance of multi-agent versus single-model approaches, the NoLiMa benchmark findings on context window degradation, and established principles from distributed systems engineering, this paper introduces the Multi-Agent Orchestration Framework (MAOF). The MAOF provides PE firms with a practical architectural pattern for decomposing deal workflows into specialized agent roles with defined handoff protocols, confidence-based human escalation, and immutable audit trails. The framework addresses the specific challenges of PE environments: heterogeneous data formats, fiduciary accountability requirements, deal confidentiality constraints, and fixed investment committee deadlines. This paper is intended for general partners, chief technology officers, operating partners, and technology advisors responsible for evaluating and deploying AI systems in investment workflows. It assumes familiarity with PE deal processes but not with AI systems architecture.</jats:p>
title: Agentic AI in Private Equity: Multi-Agent Orchestration for End-to-End Deal Workflows

items.abstract: <jats:p>Agentic AI is moving fast. Organizations are rushing to adopt autonomous workflows before they have a coherent model for how those workflows should actually be governed. The result is a pattern playing out in real time. Agents given broad access and no accountability structure fail in ways that are visible, embarrassing, and sometimes costly. This paper argues the root cause is not a capability problem. It is an organizational design problem. Drawing on practical experience designing and deploying multi-agent engineering systems, and supported by current research in agentic AI safety, human-in-the-loop design, and security, this paper proposes a framework for treating AI agents the way effective organizations treat people. Defined roles, bounded authority, structured escalation paths, and explicit accountability. The organizations that get this right will compound their productivity gains over time. The ones that skip the design work will spend that time cleaning up failures.</jats:p>
title: Agentic AI Orchestration: An Organizational Design Framework A Practitioner Framework for Reliable Multi-Agent Systems

items.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid proliferation of large language model (LLM)-based agents within productivity ecosystems has introduced a critical bottleneck: while individual agents excel at specialized tasks, efficiently orchestrating them to solve complex, multi-step workflows remains a significant challenge. Existing orchestration mechanisms often rely on rigid, rule-based routing or shallow semantic matching, which fail to capture the full breadth of possible execution paths and frequently overlook less obvious but highly relevant agent capabilities. This paper introduces a Synergistic Agentic Framework that addresses these limitations through a novel two-stage discovery and ranking mechanism. Our framework operates in two complementary phases. First, a Breadth-First Query Expansion module dynamically generates a diverse set of task interpretations and sub-goal formulations by exploring the semantic neighborhood of the user's initial query. Unlike depth-first approaches that commit to a single trajectory prematurely, this breadth-first strategy maximizes recall by exposing a wide array of potential workflow pathways and candidate agent specializations. Second, a Semantic Re-Ranking module employs dense vector embeddings and cross-encoder similarity scoring to evaluate and prioritize the expanded query set against a dynamic registry of agent capabilities and prior execution logs. This re-ranking phase ensures that precision is not sacrificed for recall, identifying the most contextually relevant and computationally efficient agent compositions. We evaluate our framework across a suite of multi-agent productivity benchmarks, encompassing document processing, data analysis, and collaborative content generation tasks. Results demonstrate that our approach achieves a 22% improvement in task completion accuracy and a 31% reduction in redundant agent invocations compared to baseline methods, including static pipelines and single-pass semantic retrievers. Furthermore, we show that the breadth-first expansion strategy is particularly effective for ambiguous or under-specified queries, where traditional systems typically fail. The synergistic combination of expansive exploration and focused re-ranking enables truly adaptive workflow orchestration, allowing the system to dynamically compose and recompose agent chains in response to intermediate results. This work contributes a principled, scalable architecture for next-generation hierarchical AI productivity networks, paving the way for more resilient, efficient, and intelligent autonomous agent ecosystems.</jats:p>
title: A Synergistic Agentic Framework Combining Breadth-First Query Expansion and Semantic Re-Ranking for Adaptive Workflow Orchestration in Multi-Agent Productivity Networks
